QUOTE: Binaries are dropped by content sniffing. Parsing is then decided per consumer: doxygen by its FILE_PATTERNS list, tree-sitter by grammar extension.
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer says that within the resolved scope, binary classification by content (not extension) drops files, and that doxygen and tree-sitter each read only the file types they support. This names the binary-classification filter and the parse-built front end.
